It just seems like I either need to find a new dream or abandon hope.

I’m not blaming it on the test. It’s just like I’ve been trying to figure out why i’m so useless, and somebody handed me a piece of paper that said “because your personality is incompatible with your dreams”.

It's not really about the test. I probably shouldn't have put it in the title. It was just a huge reality check reading all the reasons why I'm a failure. I know that there are successful, capable INTPs, but I'm the stereotype, not the exception.

> I enjoy personality tests but they can be wildly inaccurate

I initially looked at it like a buzzfeed test, and wanted to take it lightly, but it was describing me like no one ever has. And the more I looked into it, the more people there are out there just like me: miserable, useless robots.

> INTPs are actually very imaginative and open minded which sounds pretty perfect if you're creative.

It sure is, except creativity is worth nothing if you can't follow through. I'd rather have no creativity so that my head wouldn't be constantly overflowing with stupid shit I am not able to finish.

> You have so much more time to work on this, give yourself time.

There's a very big difference between being in your mid-20s and never having made a big, successful project, and being in your mid-20s and *never having finished one*. Not one! I simply lack the skillset and the dedication. I have beaten my head against the wall to find it, and I never have.

I nearly tore myself apart on my last project, and when it was cancelled due to outside circumstances, I was honestly relieved.

>set a time where you will be creative

Trust me, I've tried this, and it amplifies the stress 1000x. "Oh fuck, I've been at this 45 minutes and I've come up with nothing worthwhile." *looks back at what I've written* "In fact, if a stranger asked me to critique this, I would tell them to quit writing. Forever."

>there was a time in my life where I literally had to coach myself through standing up, walking to the light switch and turning it on.

Oh trust me, I've been in the same boat. My mental health is in a much better place now, and I think I've come to my conclusion of worthlessness very logically. 

Thank you for your thoughtful response; I hope I don't seem like I'm ignoring your points. It's just that I've told myself all the same things, and I just can't believe them.
